title: Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur partition identities in Lean

currentState.focus: Prove recurrence correctness and equality for Schur identity

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Step 7a complete. Gap/mod recurrences defined, verified for n=0..15, reduction theorem proved. 2 sorries (recurrence correctness), 3 axioms. Next: prove recurrence correctness by induction, then tackle recurrence equality.
builtItems: distinctPartGF: generating function ∏(1+X^k) as PowerSeries ℤ
schurModGF, rr1ModGF: specialized GFs for partition identities
subsetsWithSum: subset sum counting infrastructure
Bridge theorems connecting decidable ↔ noncomputable formulations
subsetsWithSum_insert_not_mem: subsets not containing k are subsets of S (proved)
subsetsWithSum_insert_mem_empty: no containing-k subsets when k > n (proved)
subsetsWithSum_insert_card: cardinality recursion (proved modulo image lemma)
distinctPartGF_coeff_empty: base case of coefficient theorem (proved)
partitionOfSubset: Finset → Nat.Partition constructor (defined, compiles)
native_decide verification extended from n=12 to n=15 for all identities
distinctPartGF_coeff: GF coefficient = subset count (Finset induction proof)
schurMod_to_subset: forward direction of SchurMod partition ↔ subset correspondence
Fixed partitionOfSubset parts_sum proof for new Mathlib API
schurModSet: {k ∈ [1..n] | k ≡ 1,2 mod 3} definition
schurMod_card_eq_subsetsWithSum: bijection via Finset.card_bij (proved)
schurMod_card_eq_gf_coeff: |schurMod n| = coeff n (schurModGF n) (proved)
schurGapSize: minimum gap function (4 if 3|m, else 3)
schurGapCount: computable recurrence for gap-side Schur partitions
schurModCount: computable recurrence for mod-side Schur partitions
schurGapBounded: decidable gap partitions with part bound
schurModBounded: decidable mod partitions with part bound
schurGapBounded_eq_full, schurModBounded_eq_full: bound=n gives full set
schurGapBounded_decompose: partitions split by max part membership
schur_from_recurrences: reduction theorem (3 subgoals → Schur identity)
insights: All 3 axioms encode deep partition identities (RR1, RR2, Schur)
Proving any axiom requires 300-500+ lines of GF proof per identity
Part XXVI (part count bounds) broke due to Mathlib API changes
Subset sum recursion: inserting element k splits subsets into containing-k and not-containing-k families
GF coefficient theorem connects algebraic (PowerSeries) to combinatorial (subsetsWithSum) counting
partitionOfSubset converts finsets to Nat.Partition, bridging subset and partition formulations
All three identities (RR1, RR2, Schur corrected) computationally verified through n=15
Proved distinctPartGF_coeff by Finset.induction: key insight is to revert n before induction so IH works for all indices. Uses PowerSeries.coeff_X_pow_mul for k≤n case and X_pow_dvd_iff for n<k case.
Proved schurMod_to_subset: convert Nodup multiset to Finset via toFinset, use Multiset.dedup_eq_self for sum equality.
PowerSeries.coeff API change: R is now implicit (use coeff (R := ℤ) n, not coeff ℤ n).
SchurMod ↔ subsetsWithSum bijection via Finset.card_bij: forward p↦parts.toFinset, inverse via partitionOfSubset
RR1/RR2 mod sides allow repeated parts (no Nodup) → distinctPartGF approach only works for Schur, not RR
schurMod_card_eq_gf_coeff chains: bijection → distinctPartGF_coeff → GF definition equality
Gap recurrence: schurGapSize(m) = 4 if m%3=0, else 3. When m≢0(mod 3), bound m-3 is valid because (m-3)≢0(mod 3).
Reduction theorem schur_from_recurrences decomposes Schur identity into 3 independent subgoals: gap correctness, mod correctness, recurrence equality.
Both recurrences verified equal for n=0..15 (48+16 native_decide examples).
Product identity approach: ∏_{k≡1,2(3)}(1+X^k) = ∏_{k≡1,5(6)}1/(1-X^k) via (1+X^k)=(1-X^{2k})/(1-X^k) and 2S⊆S cancellation
mathlibGaps: No bijective proof machinery for partition identities
nextSteps: Prove schurGapCount_eq_bounded by strong induction on (n,m): show partitions decompose as use/skip max part
Prove schurModCount_eq_bounded similarly: induction with residue filter
Prove recurrence equality (core of Schur theorem): product identity or bijection approach
Product identity path: prove (1+X^k)=(1-X^{2k})*geomPS(k), then ∏ cancellation for 2S⊆S
Alternative: build explicit bijection between schurMod and schurGapFull (Bressoud/Alladi-Gordon style)
